We make our own food. At the beginning, we leaned on a helpful website dedicated to baby food recipes and information. 

We started at 6 months with just some avocados to get him used to eating. It's a nice soft food, easy to mash and achieve the desired consistency. Then we moved on to sweet potatoes. Just throw one in the oven, cook for over an hour, cut, and blend. One makes a surprisingly large amount of servings.

Here on a popular online forum, you'll get a lot of baby-led weaning responses, but that just scares me, so we decided to do purees. It's easy. Basically, steam a vegetable in a stovetop steamer, then toss it in a mixer. We did receive a "baby food" mixer as a gift, but it was just a smaller version of the one we already had, so we don't use it.

We store them in specific containers that are great and stack nicely in the freezer. We could probably find something a bit cheaper, but these work well.

It's just important to remember that at this stage, it is basically for practice. The majority of their nutrients should be coming from milk or formula. We also learned that it is easy to overfeed, which can cause stomach pains and sleeping issues. Those couple of nights were tough. They don't need much at all; their little stomachs can't handle it.

Edit to add a suggestion: I'm not sure where you are, but look into produce companies in your area. We have one that picks the produce, flash freezes it, and sells it in bulk at an extremely discounted price. They only sell to the public every couple of months, but we got on their mailing list to be informed of those days.

It really is as simple as steaming them and then blending them really well. For more insight, go to that resource I mentioned in my original comment. While I've heard of people rejecting foods after starting with fruit, it never happened to me. Keep offering, and if that happens, eventually they will take to it.

You're at the point you need to sleep train your child. Sleep training is basically teaching them to fall asleep on their own and if they wake up, they'll be able to put themselves back to sleep. A brief description of how my partner and I did it with our two children. Both of our kids have been sleeping 12+ hours since they were 6 months old. Except for when they were sick, then all bets are off.

Get a routine. Ours included relaxation time, then bedtime where I would sing a song.

Put them in the crib tired but awake. Then I would sing my song and say goodnight. They won't like it, but leave the room. I would let them cry for a few minutes (3-5 minutes) then go back in and settle them down. Leave again, this time let them cry a little longer (maybe 7-9 minutes), then go back in and settle them down. Repeat, repeat, and eventually they fall asleep. The next night, the process will take a little less time. Then less the next day, etc.

There are many options, but we settled on this one because it seemed like common sense. If you want to check other methods, many people in parenting forums will tell you theirs is the right way and the way you want to do it is all wrong.

Good luck. STAY CONSISTENT! YOU ARE THE ADULT AND CAN WIN THE BATTLE.
